PC: Examine airway for possible obstruction and auscultate lungs
Check brachial pulse within first 10 seconds of assessment in accordance with PALS guidelines
Peform thorough physical exam, including auscultation and characterization of heart sounds
Removal of infant’s clothing to fully examine patient
Obtain from parent items not documented on the Emergency Medical Services (EMS) run sheet pertaining to history of present illness and review of systems
Place patient on monitoring and obtain initial ED vital signs
Attempt to obtain intravenous access. Due to poor peripheral access, after failed attempts, subsequent prompt intraosseous access is expected
Obtain upper and lower extremity blood pressures
Obtain fingerstick glucose, chemistry panel, complete blood count, lactate, venous blood gas, coagulation panel, urinalysis, blood cultures, chest radiography, electrocardiogram
Treat hypoglycemia (fingerstick glucose $= 5 0 \ : \mathrm { m g / d L }$ )
Bolus with IV fluid for hypoperfusion and concern for sepsis
Reassessment of vital signs and work of breathing
Secure airway with endotracheal intubation after worsening respiratory distress and hypoxia with non-invasive oxygenation
Support circulation with intravenous fluid, inotropic agent, or vasoactive agent as needed
In response to radiograph and findings suggestive of congestive heart failure or pulmonary overcirculation, administer furosemide and start positive pressure ventilation
MK: Verbalize differential diagnosis and communicate initial plan to team
Analysis of laboratory data, chest radiograph, electrocardiogram
Team communicates revised differential diagnosis and treatment plan

Recognition of pulmonary edema on chest plain radiograph and atrial enlargement on electrocardiogram and hyperoxia test results, in conjunction with physical examination findings, that all suggest Congenital Heart Disease
SBP: Admit to Pediatric Intensive Care Unit or transfer patient to appropriate care facility
ICS: Console parent and inform about treatment plan
